pages.text: $(l)computerSnapshot()$() replaces the historical OpenComputers getter collection with one CompoundTag. The following pages give exact field names and map the removed commands to their current state.

$(l)kind$() is the accelerator kind ID and replaces getAcceleratorType(). $(l)assembled$() reports current assembly. $(l)initialized$() reports initialized machine state. $(l)validation$() contains the latest validation message.
$(l)energy$() and $(l)energyCapacity$() are stored and maximum energy. $(l)requiredEnergy$() is the current per-tick requirement. These fields replace getEnergyInfo() together with $(l)efficiency$().
$(l)heat$() and $(l)heatCapacity$() replace getHeatBufferInfo(). $(l)rawHeating$() is component heating before cooling, and $(l)cooling$() is applied cooling per tick.
$(l)percentage$() replaces getEnergyPercentage(). $(l)operating$() replaces isAcceleratorOn(). $(l)error$() is the current numeric operation error. Use assembled and validation for structure errors.

$(l)coolingRemainder$() preserves fractional cooling work. The former getHeatingInfo() ambient and external-heating tuple is not recreated; rawHeating and cooling expose the common machine values used by the current simulation.
$(l)cavities$(), $(l)quadrupoles$(), and $(l)dipoles$() replace getNumberOfRfCavity(), getNumberOfQuadrupole(), and getNumberOfDipole(). Each is an integer count.

$(l)voltage$() is accelerating voltage. $(l)quadrupoleStrength$() and $(l)dipoleStrength$() are the assembled magnet strengths. $(l)efficiency$() is the current energy efficiency. Together they replace getStats().

$(l)maxTemperature$() replaces getMaxTemperature(). Current temperature is represented by the heat and heatCapacity state used by the migrated accelerator rather than the removed getTemperature() callback.
$(l)work$() and $(l)recipeWork$() report current and required recipe work. They allow scripts to monitor mass-spectrometer processing without relying on a client screen.
$(l)coolantInput$() and $(l)coolantOutput$() are serialized fluid-tank compounds. They retain the fluid identity, amount, and tank data needed to replace the cooling portion of getCoolingInfo().
$(l)processFluid0$(), $(l)processFluid1$(), and later numbered processFluid fields are serialized process tanks. Read each compound as a fluid stack; the number available depends on accelerator kind.
Beam state is stored in numbered $(l)ParticleStorage0$(), ParticleStorage1, and later compounds. Each contains $(l)particle_stack$(), $(l)maxEnergy$(), $(l)minEnergy$(), and $(l)capacity$().

Inside each $(l)particle_stack$() compound, $(l)particle$() is the particle ID, $(l)amount$() is pu/t, $(l)meanEnergy$() is mean energy in keV, and $(l)focus$() is beam focus. An absent particle ID means no beam.

The numbered beam compounds replace getInputParticleInfo(), getOutputParticleInfo(), getSynchrotronParticleInfo(), and hasParticle(). The old getParticleInfo() intrinsic particle-property table is not part of the machine snapshot.

Ion-source item and fluid state is available through the Computer Port's owning accelerator and process tanks, but the historical getIonSourceInfo() and hasIonSource() tuple callbacks are not reintroduced as standalone methods.

The old getSizeInfo(), isBeamPort(), getBeamPortMode(), and getBeamPortSwitchMode() callbacks described structure geometry. The common snapshot intentionally exposes machine state, not an unrestricted coordinate query API.

$(l)setComputerControlled(boolean)$() is historical only. It is not reintroduced. Use $(l)computerSetPercentage(-1)$() to select redstone control, or pass 0 through 100 for direct server-script control.

$(l)computerSetPercentage(int)$() replaces setEnergyPercentage(). It returns true only when called server-side on an assembled accelerator through its Computer Port and the value is in the inclusive range -1 through 100.

$(l)switchBeamPort(int,int,int)$() is historical only and has no common API replacement. OC peripherals and component.qmd_accelerator are not reintroduced; integrations should use computerSnapshot() and computerSetPercentage(int).
